text: Mangal dosha is present in this chart because Mars stands in the 1st, 2nd, 4th, 7th, 8th or 12th house counted from the Lagna, from the Moon or from Venus; the Why? inputs list which of the three references apply. The tradition reads these placements for a forthright, independent temperament that a partnership has to make room for, and the common practice is to compare both charts rather than read one alone. Each cancellation rule is shown as its own row, and the dosha is called effective only when none applies. With an unknown birth time the Lagna reference is skipped and the result is marked approx.

No Mangal dosha is present in this chart: Mars does not stand in the 1st, 2nd, 4th, 7th, 8th or 12th house counted from the Lagna, from the Moon or from Venus. The Why? inputs show Mars's sign and its house from each reference so the result can be checked. Because the rule depends on the Lagna, a chart with an unknown birth time is judged from the Moon and Venus only and carries the approx. tag. The cancellation rows are still listed so that both charts in a match are read by the same set of rules.

This cancellation applies because Mars stands in its own sign, Mesha or Vrishchika, or in its exaltation sign, Makara. A Mars at home or exalted is read as settled rather than restless, and the common rule holds that its placement in a dosha house does not then count as Mangal dosha. The row shows Mars's sign and dignity, the same dignity the planet table prints. Together with the other cancellation rows it decides whether the dosha is called effective.

This cancellation applies because Mars stands in one of the sign-and-house pairs the almanacs exempt: Mesha in the 1st house, Vrishchika in the 4th, Makara in the 7th, Karka in the 8th or Dhanu in the 12th. In each pairing the sign is held to soften what the house would otherwise mean for Mars, so the dosha is not counted. The row shows the sign and house that matched, counted from the Lagna, which is why this rule is skipped when the birth time is unknown.

This cancellation applies because Mars shares its sign with Jupiter or with the Moon. Jupiter's company is read as steadying Mars with judgement, and the Moon's as softening it with feeling, so a Mars joined by either is not counted as producing Mangal dosha. The row shows which of the two planets is with Mars. This rule uses only the planets' signs, so it applies equally when the birth time is unknown.

This cancellation applies because Jupiter aspects Mars: Mars stands in the 5th, 7th or 9th sign counted from Jupiter, which are Jupiter's full aspects by Parashara's table. An aspected Mars is read as guided rather than left to itself, and the dosha is not counted. The row shows Mars's distance from Jupiter. Because the rule works on signs alone, it applies whether or not the birth time is known.

This cancellation applies because Mars is debilitated, standing in Karka, or is combust, within its orb of the Sun. A Mars without its usual strength is held unable to produce the dosha, so the placement is not counted. The row shows which condition was met, the same debilitated and combust tags the planet table carries. This rule reads the sign and the Sun distance only, so it is independent of the birth time.

This row applies because both charts carry an effective Mangal dosha after every other rule has been checked. The tradition reads two Manglik charts as balancing each other, the classical mutual cancellation, so the pair is shown as balanced rather than one side being singled out. The row lists each side's result. When only one chart carries the dosha the row reads not applied, and the summary says plainly which chart it concerns.
